"ADHD plus movement symptoms must mean one hidden genetic cause." Two conditions can coexist without sharing a cause. Equally, "it's just ADHD" is a failure to consider the differential. Good practice is neither.

Why the difference between these matters
Levodopa tests are clues, not verdicts.
A marked levodopa response is a recognised clue toward the DRD group. Worsening on levodopa has been reported in a true VMAT2 loss-of-function condition

a.alt: Energy supply and neuronal demand. Neurons use energy to maintain gradients and support signalling.

c: Neurons use energy to maintain gradients and support signalling. This is normal physiology, not proof of an energy defect in ADHD.
MJB ADHD · original vector reconstruction · Reviewed 2026-10-13
Read the diagram explanation and sources

Aerobic metabolism supplies reducing equivalents to the respiratory chain. Proton pumping and ATP synthase couple electron transfer to ATP generation. Cells use ATP for ion homeostasis, biosynthesis and many aspects of signalling. Glycolysis also produces ATP, and fuel contributions differ with cell and context. Mitochondria do not directly manufacture dopamine. An explanation of energy supply and demand does not establish mitochondrial dysfunction or an energy deficit in an individual with ADHD.
Fuel and oxygen → Mitochondrial pathways: metabolism
Mitochondrial pathways → Proton gradient: electron transfer
ATP formation → Cellular work: ATP use
Cellular work → Demand changes: variable demand

a.alt: Mitochondrial membrane and respiratory chain. NADH supplies electrons through complex I, while succinate oxidation supplies electrons through complex II.

c: Electrons pass along the respiratory chain while complexes I, III and IV pump protons. Proton return through ATP synthase supports ATP formation. This illustrates general cell physiology; it does not establish an energy defect in a reader.
Read the diagram explanation and sources

NADH supplies electrons through complex I, while succinate oxidation supplies electrons through complex II. Ubiquinone transfers electrons to complex III, cytochrome c carries them to complex IV, and oxygen is the final acceptor. Complexes I, III and IV pump protons from the matrix towards the intermembrane space. Complex II is membrane-bound but does not pump protons; its label is placed on the matrix side in this simplified drawing. Proton return through ATP synthase supports ATP formation from ADP and phosphate. The diagram does not establish mitochondrial dysfunction in ADHD.
What this evidence can tell us
These conditions are rare. Nothing here suggests that most people with ADHD or movement symptoms have them.
